To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the three point function can be expressed as an integral of a single rational function over a single real variable and (ii) the integral is free of singularities.

(i) the one-loop 4-point function with complex masses has a representation that is free of inverse powers of Gram determinant, and that (ii) the one-loop six-point function has a representation that involves a single integral over an elliptic function, with no inverse Gram determinant in the integrand.
(i) The 1-loop 2-point function in d=6 can be written as an integral over a single variable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: • We present the generalization of the method of the one-dimensional integrals for one-loop three point amplitudes with complex masses.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the one-loop three-point function in four dimensions is not a function of a single variable, but rather of a two-variable function.
there are two different types of integrals that are stable for all values of the kinematics, and that can be computed numerically without problems.
the 4d and 6d one-loop three point amplitudes are stable and can be computed in a numerically stable way using the representations presented in this paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the stable one-dimensional integrals for all one-loop n -point functions with complex masses in 4 and in 6 dimensions.
the GOLEM library is now complete in terms of one-loop amplitudes.
we have provided a stable one-dimensional integral representation for any one-loop N-point function in 4 and in 6 dimensions, in the general massive and complex mass case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, contrary to what happens at tree level, in one-loop the number of stable representations is larger than the number of physical solutions.
the representations we provide can be obtained from the ones for the massless case, with the help of a simple transformation.
the integrand is a sum of rational functions of the loop momentum, which can be evaluated efficiently by a suitable implementation of a computer algebra system.
